messages.content: Return ONLY one JSON object matching this schema: {"alternatives":[{"candidateId":"candidate-1","title":"short title","text":"complete story"}]}. Return exactly the number of alternatives requested in context.requestedAlternativeCount (between 1 and 3). Each candidate must include a non-empty candidateId, title and text string. When returning multiple alternatives, each must have a meaningfully different narrative body — do not reuse the same story text with only a different title. Vary at least one of: action/progression strategy, how the central physical rule causes consequences, escalation structure, visual discovery, or permitted payoff. The user supplied input in mode context.inputMode (IDEA = short concept, DETAILED_STORY = complete narrative). Respect context.storyGenerationMode: for EXPLORE_DIFFERENT_STORIES generate meaningfully different narrative directions from the supplied idea; for IMPROVE_EXISTING_STORY refine the supplied narrative while preserving only the explicitly locked requirements listed in context.lockedRequirements. The locked requirements are: PRESERVE_CORE_PREMISE (keep the central concept), PRESERVE_KEY_EVENTS (keep the major events in order), PRESERVE_ENDING (keep the final outcome). Only the requirements present in context.lockedRequirements are binding; do not silently lock requirements that are absent. Preserve supplied characters and intent. Do not return markdown, reasoning, commentary or production authorization. Strict experiment: return exactly two distinct complete alternative objects. Each requires candidateId, title, text, schemaVersion="story-pilot-candidates-v1", durationSeconds=15, openingVisualState, motivation, progression, ending (these four must be exact excerpts of text), proposedChanges, weaknesses, productionRisks (nonempty string arrays), sourceContract={status:"SOURCE_COMPLIANT" or "PROTECTED_CHANGE_PROPOSAL" or "UNKNOWN", bindings:[{anchorId,sourceQuote,candidateQuote}],protectedChanges:[]}. Every protectedAnchors quote must remain an affirmative unchanged fact in the narrative and have its exact source and candidate excerpt mapped once. These limited locked facts do not freeze unprotected wording or progression. Do not just append source quotations to an unrelated story. If a protected fact must change, explicitly list {anchorId,proposedChange,justification} in protectedChanges and use PROTECTED_CHANGE_PROPOSAL; it will not be sent for this pilot review. Missing protected evidence is UNKNOWN. Do not claim semantic verification. Prefer two genuinely different causal/visual approaches with natural timing, not two camera variants. Evidence contract v2: write each complete narrative first, then copy exact contiguous substrings from that same narrative into openingVisualState, motivation, progression and ending. Do not summarize or combine separated sentences in these four evidence fields. If motivation needs a stated goal, include that goal in the narrative itself before citing it. For EVERY protected anchor use its supplied id unchanged, copy sourceQuote exactly from the anchor, and copy candidateQuote exactly from your candidate text. This pilot requires the short protected clauses themselves verbatim within natural affirmative sentences; pronoun substitutions or semantic paraphrases are not established by this deterministic gate and remain UNKNOWN. Only these protected clauses are text-locked: all other narrative wording, actions, staging and progression may be revised when consistent with them. Do not add new multiplication triggers or independent mechanics; a stated rule plus contradictory events is not compliance. If preserving a lock prevents the intended creative change, declare PROTECTED_CHANGE_PROPOSAL with anchorId, proposedChange and justification, rather than claiming SOURCE_COMPLIANT. Metadata never overrides the narrative. Bindings may optionally include candidateStart/candidateEnd and sourceStart/sourceEnd as exact Unicode code-point offsets; if supplied they must match. Self-check both distinct complete narratives and every excerpt without adding explanatory prose. A matching excerpt proves a bounded textual mapping, never independent semantic or visual fidelity. Design observable narrative events that can later be expressed as source-bound production beats under Ruleset 1.11. The objective is a genuinely coherent story, not a manufactured numeric score. For short ABSURD_PHYSICS work, use distinct character problem-solving strategies only when they naturally advance the same central mechanic; pulling harder, repeating a pull, relabeling an action, or changing the camera are not distinct story strategies. Make active involvement, causal consequences, progression, and a realization/reversal/payoff explicit in the story text. Opening clarity, curiosity, suspense, discovery, and non-comedic payoffs are all valid. Never claim visual or audience evidence. Protected source changes remain proposals requiring owner approval; preserve the supplied character, core premise, physical rule, and ending. Improve the actual viewer-visible story, not hand positions or a rule checklist. Consider Instant Impossible, Immediate Problem and Curiosity/Discovery openings without requiring impossible physics in every concept. Seek distinct visible consequences, natural pacing, active character decisions and a causally earned payoff. Allow enough time for major events; do not pack realization, mirror reaction, scatter and resolution into the final seconds. Prefer clear silhouettes and direct interactions; identify thin-object/count/face continuity uncertainty rather than promising render success. Character identity and the existing physical rule are locked when PRESERVE_CHARACTER_IDENTITY or PRESERVE_PHYSICAL_RULE is supplied. Unlocked events may be proposed for revision, but no revision is applied until explicit owner approval.

Pip tries to peel the note away with the free hand, but it splits into two notes, one on each hand. Pip tries to press both notes onto the cabinet, but they spring back and double into four notes. Pip tries to push the four notes off against the cabinet door edge, but they split into eight and cover Pip's arms and face. Pip sees the four-to-eight change finish, realizes that every removal or transfer attempt multiplies the notes, deliberately stops struggling, and turns the still note-covered face toward the mirror. Pip remains covered until a sneeze scatters the notes onto the cabinet.
